jobs.title: Engineering Manager - MLOps & Analytics
jobs.jd_full:
The role of an Engineering Manager at Canonical

As an Engineering Manager at Canonical, you must be technically strong, but your main responsibility is to run an effective team and develop the colleagues you manage. You will develop and review code as a leader, while at the same time staying aware of that the best way to improve the product is to ensure that the whole team is focused, productive and unblocked.

You are expected to help them grow as engineers, do meaningful work, do it outstandingly well, find professional and personal satisfaction, and work well with colleagues and the community. You will also be expected to be a positive influence on culture, facilitate technical delivery, and regularly reflect with your team on strategy and execution.

You will collaborate closely with other Engineering Managers, product managers, and architects, producing an engineering roadmap with ambitious and achievable goals.

We expect Engineering Managers to be fluent in the programming language, architecture, and components that their team uses, in this case popular open-source machine learning tools like Kubeflow, MLFlow, and Feast.

Code reviews and architectural leadership are part of the job. The commitment to healthy engineering practices, documentation, quality and performance optimisation is as important, as is the requirement for fair and clear management, and the obligation to ensure a high-performing team.

Location: This is a Globally remote role.

 

What your day will look like

  • Manage a distributed team of engineers and its MLOps/Analytics portfolio
  • Organize and lead the team’s processes in order to help it achieve its objectives
  • Conduct one-on-one meetings with team members
  • Identify and measure team health indicators
  • Interact with a vibrant community
  • Review code produced by other engineers
  • Attend conferences to represent Canonical and its MLOps solutions
  • Mentor and grow your direct reports, helping them achieve their professional goals
  • Work from home with global travel for 2 to 4 weeks per year for internal and external events 

What we are looking for in you

  • A proven track record of professional experience of software delivery
  • Professional python development experience, preferably with a track record in open source
  • A proven understanding of the machine learning space, its challenges and opportunities to improve
  • Experience designing and implementing MLOps solutions
  • An exceptional academic track record from both high school and preferably university
  • Willingness to travel up to 4 times a year for internal events

Additional skills that you might also bring

The following skills may be helpful to you in the role, but we don't expect everyone to bring all of them.

  • Hands-on experience with machine learning libraries, or tools.
  • Proven track record of building highly automated machine learning solutions for the cloud.
  • Experience with building machine learning models
  • Experience with container technologies (Docker, LXD, Kubernetes, etc.)
  • Experience with public clouds (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud)
  • Experience in the Linux and open-source software world
  • Working knowledge of cloud computing
  • Passionate about software quality and testing
  • Experience working on a distributed team on an open source project -- even if that is community open source contributions.
  • Demonstrated track record of Open Source contributions

What we offer you

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognise outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus. We provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

 

  • Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!
  • Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues from your team and others
  • Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Beacon Biosignals is transforming precision medicine for the brain, from clinical development to clinical care. For Life Sciences partners, we offer the leading at-home EEG platform for clinical development of novel therapeutics for neurological, psychiatric, and sleep disorders. Our Diagnostics business is building the most comprehensive at-home platform for precision diagnostics, combining EEG and cardiopulmonary signals to deliver reimbursable assessments for sleep and central nervous system disorders. Together, we’re changing the way patients are diagnosed and treated for any disorder that affects brain physiology.

What you will be doing:

In this exciting and challenging role as a Technical Product Manager, you will drive the definition and execution of next-generation medical devices that meet user needs, clinical requirements, business objectives, and regulatory expectations. You will be part of the Device Team, reporting to the Director of Device Engineering and working closely with systems, hardware, firmware, software, algorithm, manufacturing, quality, and clinical teams. You will own product requirements, user needs, product roadmaps, usability activities, and design control deliverables while ensuring alignment between customer needs and engineering execution.

Your goal as a Technical Product Manager is to deliver innovative, reliable, and user-centered medical devices by translating customer and clinical insights into clear product requirements and development priorities. You will lead cross-functional product planning from concept through commercialization, balancing user experience, technical feasibility, manufacturing readiness, regulatory requirements, cost, and schedule. You will coordinate product development activities, facilitate technical tradeoff discussions, and ensure stakeholders remain aligned throughout the product lifecycle.

This is a fully remote role from anywhere in the U.S. Beacon’s robust asynchronous work practices ensure a first-class remote work experience, while also providing in-person office hubs located in Paris, Boston, New York, and the San Francisco Bay Area.

What success looks like:

  • Own product requirements, user needs, intended use, and system-level product definition for a major device product line.
  • Translate customer needs, clinical requirements, technical constraints, and business objectives into actionable product requirements and development roadmaps.
  • Partner closely with Systems, Hardware, Firmware, Software, Algorithms, Clinical, Quality, Regulatory, Business Development, Operations, and Manufacturing teams to drive successful product development and commercialization.
  • Lead cross-functional tradeoff discussions involving functionality, usability, technical risk, manufacturability, regulatory requirements, cost, and schedule.
  • Drive product development through concept, feasibility, verification, validation, manufacturing transfer, and sustaining engineering.
  • Coordinate usability studies, customer evaluations, clinical feedback activities, and product validation efforts.
  • Support design control activities, including user needs, requirements traceability, risk management, design reviews, and regulatory documentation.
  • Drive day-to-day Agile product development practices across multiple initiatives and product portfolios within a product line.
  • Collaborate with suppliers, contract manufacturers, and external partners to support product development, manufacturing readiness, and product launches.
  • Communicate product status, key decisions, risks, and roadmap updates to stakeholders and leadership.

What you will bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
  • 5–8 years of experience in product management, systems engineering, device development, or related technical leadership roles.
  • At least 3 years of experience supporting the development and commercialization of hardware, medical devices, wearables, or other multidisciplinary products.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate customer, clinical, and business needs into product requirements, roadmaps, and development priorities.
  • Experience working closely with hardware, firmware, software, systems, manufacturing, and quality teams throughout the product development lifecycle.
  • Experience supporting products through design controls, verification and validation, manufacturing transfer, and commercialization activities.
  • Strong technical aptitude with the ability to understand engineering tradeoffs involving functionality, usability, reliability, manufacturability, cost, and schedule.
  • Strong communication, organizational, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to drive alignment across cross-functional teams.
  • Experience working in regulated industries, including medical devices, healthcare technology, or other safety-critical products preferred.
  • Experience with modern product development and collaboration tools such as Ketryx, Jira, Figma, GitHub, Asana, or similar tools preferred.

The salary range for this role is $160,000 – $183,000. Salary ranges are determined using current market compensation data for this role and adjusted based on experience, skills, and location. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package, which includes equity, PTO and other benefits.

At Beacon, we’ve found that cultural and scientific impact is driven most by those who lead by example. As such, we’re always seeking new contributors whose work demonstrates an avid curiosity, a bias towards simplicity, an eye for composability, a self-service mindset, and - most of all - a deep empathy towards colleagues, stakeholders, users, and patients. We believe a diverse team builds more robust systems and achieves higher impact.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.jd_full:
Location: Europe (Remote)

Status: Full-Time | Permanent | Exempt Status

Pay: USD $50,000 - $60,000

Requirement: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience

We are seeking a detail-oriented and motivated Product Manager to join our team. In this role, you will own the daily product loops across Central and pZero, translating user evidence and stakeholder input into requirements, priorities, and rollout plans. The ideal candidate will have hands-on product or UX design experience, strong written communication, and the ability to partner closely with engineering and cross-functional teams. No production frontend coding is required for this position.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the daily product loop for Central and pZero, from user evidence and problem definition through requirements, delivery, rollout, and adoption.
  • Translate user evidence and stakeholder input into clear product briefs and PRDs, including problem, scope, exclusions, success measures, and acceptance criteria.
  • Lead product design for core Central and pZero workflows, including journey mapping, information architecture, prototyping in Figma or an equivalent tool, and usability testing.
  • Partner with the external engineering team throughout delivery, clarifying requirements and keeping work moving through review and release.
  • Bring Product Quality into the work early enough to shape journeys, testability, and release evidence.
  • Own rollout and adoption for shipped features, ensuring intended users can find, understand, and use new functionality.
  • Track product outcomes after release, including adoption, task completion, cycle time, rework, defects, support burden, and the amount of follow-up required from the Director of Product.
  • Own manager-facing and worker-facing product documentation, including onboarding materials, tutorials, how-to guides, and release education.
  • Maintain a practical, shared design foundation with Iron Forge covering navigation, forms, tables, statuses, errors, permissions, accessibility, and responsive behavior.
  • Maintain shared product knowledge in company-approved project and knowledge management systems, including roadmap, decisions, user evidence, product behavior, and release learning.
  • Use approved AI tools and shared skills to improve the speed and quality of research, writing, analysis, prototyping, and documentation.
  • Collect and prioritize input from Operations, Product Quality, Engineering, support signals, and client programs.
  • Bring well-supported recommendations, backed by evidence and tradeoffs, to the Director of Product on major product decisions, while owning routine and reversible decisions independently.
  • Perform other duties and ad-hoc projects as assigned.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience in product management or a closely related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience as a product owner or product manager, ideally within AI workforce product; scope of ownership matters more than years of tenure.
  • Hands-on product or UX design experience, ideally including journey mapping, prototyping, and usability testing.
  • Proven ability to turn incomplete or conflicting stakeholder input into a clear, bounded product problem.
  • Experience working closely with engineering teams as a partner, not solely through ticket handoffs.
  • Comfort using data to make or evaluate decisions, including recognizing when available data is insufficient.
  • Experience owning outcomes after release, including adoption, documentation, and iteration based on real usage.
  • Working familiarity with AI tools for research, writing, prototyping, and documentation, with clear human review and accountability.
  • Strong written communication skills, able to produce material that developers, operators, managers, and users can act on directly.
  • Ability to work effectively across distributed teams and manage ambiguity without creating unnecessary noise.
  • Comfortable inspecting product behavior, reading technical material, and working with data; production coding is not required.
  • Cross-functional collaboration and conflict resolution skills, with the decisiveness expected of a single-threaded owner.

Requirements

  • Ability to work in a quiet, professional environment free from distractions to support productivity and confidentiality.
  • Must be able to appear on camera for video calls and communicate clearly in virtual meetings.
  • Ability to provide valid documentation verifying identity and authorization to work in the United States or applicable hiring location.
  • Flexibility to adjust schedules based on project needs, with occasional requests for additional hours during temporary projects.

Physical Requirements

  • Occasional travel may be required for special meetings, training, or team gatherings at the company’s headquarters or other designated locations.
  • Routine use of standard office equipment such as computers, phones, filing cabinets, etc.
    • Strong visual acuity for reviewing detailed documents and data on computer screens.
    • Manual dexterity for operating a computer, including using a keyboard and mouse.
    • Ability to lift and carry office supplies or equipment weighing up to 25 pounds.
    • Clear verbal and written communication skills for collaboration across teams.
    • Capacity to manage tasks that require prolonged periods of focus and concentration.
    • Ability to handle the physical demands of a standard workweek, which may include occasional overtime, nights, weekends, and holidays, if needed.

About Us

As a global data company, Productive Playhouse “PPH”, is pioneering our approach to language and data services, while incorporating their roots as a production company. Originally creating content to support children’s language acquisition, our commitment to excellence, forward-thinking strategies, and world-wide cultural experience has proven key for delivering exceptional service.

Originally founded as an educational production company, Productive Playhouse made a mark with our award winning children’s series, which taught fundamental subjects through engaging and effective programming. This early success paved the way for our evolution into a comprehensive data services provider.

Since 2011, Productive Playhouse has expanded rapidly to offer an extensive suite of data services. Our current offerings include transcription, translation, linguistic analysis, rating, systems testing, localization, field and studio recording, language skill verification, and specialized data handling with a focus on sensitivity and diversity. Our commitment to innovation means we continually enhance our service portfolio to meet the evolving needs of our clients.

At Productive Playhouse, we are proud of our reputation for addressing complex challenges with agility and delivering premium, secure data solutions across diverse environments. Our dynamic team is dedicated to maintaining the highest standards and ensuring exceptional service every time.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Network Facilities
jobs.jd_full:
At gFiber, we believe that great internet has the power to drive innovation, strengthen communities, enable the impossible, and do all the everyday things that make all of our world go round. And the job of creating better internet is never done - so we’re growing! Our team is committed to building a place where people who want to make a difference can grow their careers and find their spot to belong.

The application window will be open until at least September 27th, 2026. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the specified date.

This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Role Description

As a Technical Program Manager, you will lead and optimize complex, ambiguous, and often undefined programs that have significant organizational impact. You will balance near-term deliverables with long-term strategy, navigating delivery challenges and opportunities in rapidly evolving environments. You will partner and strategize with leadership to seek out and drive collaborations across organizational boundaries, leveraging your technical judgment to inform strategic thinking and operational effectiveness.

In this role, you’ll:

  • Define and drive strategic, ambiguous programs and processes that address significant challenges with cross product-area impact.
  • Spearhead efforts to drive consistency, efficiency, and economies of scale across infrastructure workstreams.
  • Partner with leadership across multiple functions to align on differing objectives and drive collaborations across organizational boundaries.
  • Build and implement innovative solutions to improve operational effectiveness, identifying process breakdowns and anticipating/responding dynamically to change.
  • Develop technical roadmaps and white papers alongside engineering stakeholders to provide data-driven influence on technical decision-making.
  • Coach, mentor, and provide guidance to team members, setting best practices for program management within the organization.

At a minimum, we would like you to have:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5 years experience in a service provider or enterprise network working with competency in several core and/or access networking concepts, including TCP/IP, BGP, OSPF, MPLS, ELINE/ELAN/EVPN, and physical layer technologies (fiber optics, DWDM, transceivers) and AC/DC power systems.
  • 2 years of technical program management or equivalent experience, specifically leading complex, cross-functional, and high-impact programs.
  • Expertise in building and maintaining effective program teams and establishing best practices to drive continuous improvement.
  • Ability to travel domestically up to 25%

It’s preferred that you have:

  • Proficiency in instantiating highly scalable core and access networks in an active service-provider or enterprise environment
  • Direct experience provisioning/operating/troubleshooting one or more of Juniper, Cisco, Arista, Nokia, or Ciena network equipment in a service provider or medium to large enterprise environment.
  • Experience with basic network space planning (Rack face elevations, floorplans, electrical and heat density, etc).
  • Experience in leading and managing program portfolios across broader organizations or Product Areas.
  • Technical judgment and understanding, with experience influencing architectural and structural decisions.
  • Experience in identifying systemic issues and translating them into actionable, long-term transformational initiatives.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Integrations (Ad Platforms / CRM)
jobs.jd_full:
The Position

CallRail is looking for a Senior Product Manager to own one of our most important integration domains — either our ad platform integrations (Google Ads, Microsoft Advertising, Meta) or our CRM integrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, and the vertical systems our customers run their businesses on).

These integrations are where CallRail’s data becomes real value for customers: closing the loop between a phone call and the ad that drove it, or pushing conversation intelligence into the system a sales team actually works in. You’ll lead the strategy for your domain and own that surface end to end, and partner with the other integrations PM on the shared patterns — data sync, authentication, webhooks, and third-party APIs — so the portfolio stays coherent.

Your integrations are also the foundation other teams build on — including Voice Assist, where what our AI agents can do for a customer depends directly on what your integrations can read and write.

We’re looking for someone who is genuinely AI-fluent — both in how they work and in what they build. The integration landscape is changing fast: platforms are exposing agent-accessible interfaces, customers expect setup and mapping to be intelligent rather than manual, and the PMs who move fastest are the ones using AI as a daily tool rather than a talking point. You don’t need to be an ML engineer. You do need to reach for AI first and have opinions about where it helps and where it doesn’t.

This role suits a self-motivated PM who thrives at both setting product direction and rolling up their sleeves to deliver results with engineering.

What You’ll Do

Own your integration domain

  • Define and own some of our largest core integrations, aligning them with business goals, customer needs, and strategic partnerships.
  • Take the integrations customers already depend on past MVP — fill functional gaps, expand data coverage, and make them genuinely good rather than merely connected.
  • Own how customers experience your domain: how they discover, connect, configure, and troubleshoot the integrations you’re responsible for.
  • Lead discovery with customers, partners, and internal teams to validate problems before scoping solutions.

Lead the strategy

  • Lead the product strategy for your integration domain — synthesizing input from Partnerships, business strategy, and customer signal into a clear point of view, and driving alignment on it across the org.
  • Partner with the other integrations PM on the shared design patterns every integration inherits — data sync, authentication, webhooks, and third-party APIs — and make sure the next integration is cheaper to build than the last.
  • Stay current with partner platform roadmaps and the shifting privacy and measurement landscape, and bring a point of view on what it means for our customers.

Bring AI into the product

  • Identify where AI meaningfully improves the integration experience — intelligent field mapping, automated setup and diagnostics, enriched data pushed into partner systems, self-healing syncs — and build the case for what’s worth investing in.
  • Shape how CallRail’s integration data is consumed by AI agents and assistants, as customers increasingly expect their systems to be queryable and actionable by AI rather than only by humans.
  • Know the difference between an AI feature that holds up in production and one that demos well, and be willing to say so.

Prioritize and measure

  • Monitor success metrics, product health, and user feedback, and use them to continuously refine your domain.
  • Make the call on sequencing net-new work against fixes and migrations, and be able to explain that call to anyone who asks.
  • Keep the unglamorous half of integration work — bugs, migrations, reliability — visible and scheduled rather than invisible and endless.

Cross-functional

  • Partner with other product teams whose features depend on your integrations — most often Voice Assist, where the quality of a CRM or scheduling integration directly determines what our AI agents can actually do for a customer. Treat your domain as a platform other teams build on, and sequence your roadmap accordingly.
  • Work closely with Product Design on the integration experience — setup and authentication flows, field mapping, error and reconnection states — where most of the design difficulty is in making genuinely complex configuration feel simple.
  • Write clear, actionable epics, user stories, and acceptance criteria with real technical context and edge cases identified up front.
  • Partner with Marketing, Sales, and Customer Experience on launches, enablement, and adoption of new integrations.
  • Close the loop with Support — turn ticket patterns into prioritized work, and give them answers and workarounds in the meantime.
  • Represent the integrations domain in planning cycles, executive updates, and cross-functional initiatives.

What You’ll Need

  • 5+ years of product management experience, with 2+ years focused on integrations, partner ecosystems, or platform-oriented work.

Deep API design experience isn’t required, but you need to know this territory well enough to make good calls about rate limits, sync behavior, and failure modes.

Working With AI at CallRail

AI is core to how our product team operates, and we expect it to be core to how you operate. We use Claude across discovery, spec writing, data analysis, prototyping, and internal tooling, and we’re actively building AI capabilities into the product itself. In this role you will:

  • Use AI daily as a working tool — clustering support tickets to find the real bug patterns, drafting and pressure-testing specs, exploring integration data, and building throwaway scripts and prototypes to answer questions faster than a meeting could.
  • Build your own leverage rather than waiting for it — writing Claude skills, agents, and internal workflows that make you and your team faster.
  • Think about CallRail’s platform as something AI agents will consume, not just humans. MCP servers, agent-friendly API design, and tool-calling patterns are increasingly part of what a modern integrations platform is expected to offer, and you’ll help shape our point of view there.
  • Stay genuinely current. The tooling changes every few months, and we want someone curious enough to keep up and pragmatic enough to know when a new tool actually helps.

We’re looking for evidence that you’ve already changed how you work because of these tools — not just enthusiasm about them.

If you do not meet all the requirements listed, we still encourage you to apply! No job description is perfect, and we may also have another opportunity that aligns with your skills and experience.

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Shopping Experience
jobs.jd_full:
The Role:

As a digitally native company, Minted’s Shopping Experience and commerce platform are core to the company’s success. Minted’s online shopping experience allows consumers to discover, customize, and purchase from an extensive assortment of products and categories, all designed by independent artists around the world. We are driven by creating a customer journey that serves both our artist community and the savvy e-commerce shopper.

We are seeking a Lead Product Manager to own the strategy for how customers find and choose products on Minted. Over the next two years, we are integrating a new product information management platform, which will give us structured, machine-readable data about our product catalog. That data supports a set of experiences we cannot build today: search and browse that understand what a customer is looking for, product detail and category pages generated from product attributes, and filtered navigation that is fully crawlable. Combined with parallel investments in analytics, customer data, and content management, it is the foundation for conversational shopping and for deep personalization later. This role decides what we build on that foundation, in what order, and why.

The role spans our discovery surfaces (search, browse, category, and product detail) and our conversion optimization program, with dependencies running into product data, customization and rendering, checkout, and marketing. You will set the strategy and objectives for your pod, lead initiatives that cross pod and functional boundaries, and raise the standard of product craft for the PMs around you.

You will:

  • Set the strategy for Minted’s discovery experience in partnership with engineering and design: where to play and how to win across search, browse, category, and product detail. Derive it from business strategy, the competitive environment, behavioral data, test results, customer insight, and technical constraints and capabilities.
  • Prioritize the growth levers that move our targets, then prioritize the customer problems that move those levers, then consider the solution space. Up-level the organization by holding that sequence when others want to start with solutions.
  • Set the objectives, key results, roadmap, and initiative scope consistent with that strategy, along with the sequencing and the resourcing implications. Carry a two-year planning view alongside the near-term roadmap.
  • Own and continuously maintain the prioritized list of customer problems across your surfaces, keeping it current with fresh behavioral data, user research, customer support and concierge signals, session replay, dogfooding, and competitive scans.
  • Define the strategy for turning our new product data foundation into customer value, and lead its execution: attribute-driven search and browse, dynamic product detail and category pages, crawlable filtered navigation, and the groundwork for conversational shopping and deeply personalized discovery.
  • Develop and lead initiative strategies that span multiple teams and functions, and resolve the dependencies and disagreements those initiatives create with other teams and with stakeholders.
  • Shape solutions with engineering and design. You hold the business problem and the value case, design holds the experience, engineering holds feasibility and cost. Your job is to find the right-sized solution where the three meet.
  • Argue for defensibility in addition to value. Ask whether a bet is hard for a competitor to copy and whether it improves margin, and be willing to kill an idea that does not clear the bar.
  • Set a new standard for rationale and foresight with the briefs and documentation you produce, stating the assumptions, the growth lever, the customer problem, the success criteria, and the instrumentation plan explicitly.
  • Specify the instrumentation for everything your team ships, including the events that power key metrics and KPIs and the tracking behind on-site clicks and interactions. Instrumentation is called out explicitly in the brief and ships with the work.
  • Run a high-velocity test program across your surfaces. Design lean tests with the intent to launch and productionize them if they win. Evangelize the tenets of proper experiment design and lead by example in your understanding of what is working or not working, why, and what to do about it.
  • Manage upward with clear strategic intent and a recommendation attached to every problem you raise, and get out in front of risks and stakeholder misalignment before they escalate.
  • Be the trusted and accountable partner to your teammates and stakeholders. Run project kickoffs and read-outs, prioritize and revise the backlog through delivery, handle scope changes, prepare Customer Service and other affected teams ahead of launch, and run user acceptance testing to ensure quality output.
  • Report results broadly against objectives and KPIs, share the insight across teams, and decide how each result reshapes your roadmap.
  • Mentor and develop other product managers on their craft, and participate in hiring. Raise the standard for problem framing, briefs, instrumentation, and experiment analysis on the team around you.

You are:

  • Problem-first. You start with a clearly framed problem statement, align others on its priority and its connection to customer and business outcomes, and hold the line on agreeing on the top two or three problems before moving to solutions.
  • A strategic, consumer-centric thinker. You have a theory of the customer. You can explain why a metric moved and what is happening inside the experience, grounded in behavioral data, research, and direct observation.
  • Fluent in the business. You start from the objective and the margin logic, you can connect any experience change to the number it moves, and you understand how Minted makes money well enough to teach it.
  • Data-driven. You own the metrics for your area, keep a continuous health check on them, and propose hypotheses to improve them.
  • Realistic about win rates. Not every launch or experiment will win on the first try. You build time to iterate inside a problem space and treat a single test as a data point.
  • A systems thinker. You understand how the tech stack, the data model, and the customer journey fit together, and you are technical enough to reason about feasibility, complexity, and architectural tradeoffs with engineers.
  • Able to create clarity out of ambiguity. Given an unstructured pile of input from disparate sources, you produce a framework for the decision and a plan for execution.
  • Effective without authority. You lead engineering and design partners, peer teams, and senior stakeholders through credibility, clear problem framing, narrative, and evidence. You understand a partner’s goals before you negotiate a tradeoff, and you use data to settle the tension.
  • Decisive. You break choices into explicit options so people know what is being decided, land the decision with an owner and a next step, and secure commitment from the people who disagreed.
  • A multiplier. You coach and give feedback to other PMs, share credit, co-create with partners so they own the outcome with you, and let engineering and design lead in their own areas.
  • Detail-oriented. You identify and resolve edge cases along with functional and aesthetic details to deliver a quality experience.
  • Curious and gritty. You get into the details of real customer behavior, understand their motivations, and stay on a problem until you understand it.
  • Accountable for your own output, including the parts AI helped produce. You use AI to think, elaborate, and stress-test your reasoning, but you own the judgment and the final artifact.
  • Transparent and humble. You say what you do not know and what you got wrong. You invite partners to engage on the answer because the best outcomes happen when all viewpoints are considered.

You have:

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • 8+ years of product management experience building and shipping successful consumer e-commerce or direct-to-consumer products and features
  • A track record of setting product strategy for a team or surface area, and accountability for the outcome it produced
  • Experience leading initiatives that span multiple teams and functions, including the dependency and stakeholder work that comes with them
  • Direct experience owning discovery surfaces: search, browse, navigation, category, or product detail pages
  • Experience building or materially improving an experimentation program, including test design, correct result interpretation, and diagnosis of measurement and data quality problems
  • Superb analytical skills and fluency with the tools used to investigate customer behavior
  • Demonstrated understanding of technology and architecture, and effective partnership with engineering to identify technical solutions based on tradeoffs across user experience, technical debt, latency, scalability, reliability, and time to market
  • Experience mentoring or developing other product managers
  • Working fluency with AI tools in your daily product practice
  • Project management skills: ability to plan, set expectations, make and meet commitments, and provide structure and process to cross-functional teams
  • Intense commitment to the quality of the product and customer experience

Bonus Points For:

  • MBA or Master’s degree in a relevant field
  • Experience with a product information management platform, structured product taxonomy, or attribute-driven merchandising
  • Experience with a hosted search and discovery platform
  • Technical SEO or answer engine optimization experience
  • Experience with personalization or recommendation systems
  • Experience in a two-sided marketplace
  • Experience through a platform replatforming or migration of comparable scope

Compensation:

The compensation range for the role applies to employment offers from Minted. Our employment offers fall between the minimum and midpoint of the range to allow for continued salary growth during your employment at Minted. The upper half of the range accommodates this growth and supports our intention to create an environment that encourages lasting relationships between Minted and our employees.

Minted utilizes a market-based compensation model with four geographic tiers. Final compensation is determined based on the candidate’s primary work location, defined as their residence within 60 miles of a metropolitan area:

Geo 1: New York, NY; Los Angeles, CA & all other California markets - $143,888 - $188,853

Geo 2: Boston, MA; Washington, DC; Chicago, IL; Seattle, WA; Austin, TX; Atlanta, GA; Portland, OR - $132,940 - $174,484

Geo 3: All other U.S. metro locations - $121,992 - $160,115

Salaries will vary based on various factors, including but not limited to professional and academic experience, associated job responsibilities, and/or other business or organizational needs.

This role is eligible for stock options.

Benefits:

Benefits will be effective on the first of each month following your initial hire date.

- Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits

- Employer-Funded Health Savings Account

- 10 Paid Holidays

- Paid Time Off and Sick Leave

- Paid Parental Leave

- Monthly Gym/Wellness Reimbursement

- 401(k) retirement savings plan

- Employer-Funded Commuter Benefits

- Friends and Family Discount

DISCLAIMER:

We verify identity at the start of interviews to ensure fairness and security. We reserve the right to withdraw candidates who misrepresent their identity, experience, or qualifications at any stage of the process.

Notice of AI Use in Employment Decisions:

We use AI-powered tools, including Brainner AI, to support our hiring and employment processes. These tools help assess job-related qualifications and improve efficiency, but all decisions involve human review.

About Minted:

Artists shape culture. They spark conversation, create connection, and bring beauty into the world. Minted is where they come together to reach further. Our marketplace empowers a thriving community of independent artists to sell and scale their work. We nurture self-expression, cultivate community, and bring the best in visual art to a global audience.

We’re building a new way to discover the world’s best creative talent. We’re here for the emerging talent ready to take off, the local favorites ready to grow, and the established artists ready to dream bigger.

At Minted, our people don’t just believe in the power of art–we live it. We have our finger on the pulse of what’s new and now. We’re obsessed with great design, art, and interiors. We’re in galleries, at fairs, and constantly finding inspiration online. We seek undiscovered talent that deserves to stand up and stand out. We connect with artists that have something to say, and we collaborate to amplify their work.  The Minted community’s art, stationery, and textiles products have reached over 75 million homes worldwide.

Our marketplace brings the best in independent design to consumers everywhere. We recognize the challenges independent artists face, and we leverage our resources to level the playing field and create a platform that gives artists the freedom to develop their craft and grow their business.

We are headquartered in San Francisco, CA and currently employ 350+ full-time employees, plus additional temporary workers during the holiday season. We have raised over $300M from top-tier investors including Benchmark Capital, T. Rowe Price, Permira, Ridge Ventures, Technology Crossover Ventures, and Norwest Venture Partners.  Angel investors include Marissa Mayer, Jeremy Stoppelman, Julia & Kevin Hartz, Yishan Wong, and more.

Minted is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to inclusion and diversity. We welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives and will consider all qualified applicants for employment in accordance with all state, local, and federal laws. Minted participates in the E-verify program.

How Our Process Works:

Minted uses technology and innovative practices to bring unique, best-selling design to market at scale. Using its crowdsourcing technology, consumers are empowered to vote for the designs they love and want to see sold, ensuring that Minted always sells continuously fresh and trend-forward product. The winning designs are manufactured by Minted, enabling artists from around the world to share and sell their work while letting Minted do the rest. Since launch in 2007, the company has expanded to serve consumers in new categories including wall art, textiles, digital content and home decor, as well as serve major retailers and consumer products brands with data-backed design through licensing and wholesale partnerships.

jobs.title: Sr. Project Manager, Interconnection Projects & Grid Infrastructure Delivery
jobs.jd_full:
Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.

We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.

Position Summary

Antora is seeking a Manager, Interconnection Projects & Grid Infrastructure Delivery to own the delivery of interconnection engineering, SCADA and telemetry systems, and grid infrastructure for Antora’s thermal energy storage projects across multiple RTOs/ISOs. This is a hands-on role: the person in this seat will write/validate the statements of work, hold the budget, set the schedule, and hold consultants, Owner’s Engineers and EPC firms to deliverables that are technically defensible.

The ideal candidate combines practical program management discipline, scope definition, cost and schedule control, change management with enough engineering fluency to interrogate a data point list, an architecture diagram or an interface control document and recognize what is missing. The role works across Antora’s portfolio in MISO, SPP, ERCOT and PJM, and partners closely with interconnection and grid engineering, project development, product engineering, legal and finance.

Roles & Responsibilities

  • Interconnection Engineering & Infrastructure Delivery

    • Manage engineering firms from concept through issued-for-construction design, covering substations, switchyards, POI configurations, protection and control, metering, grounding, and equipment specifications. Optimize configurations for reliability and cost.
    • Ensure designs incorporate interconnection studies and GIA/LGIA/DIA obligations; resolve changes affecting design, cost, or schedule.
    • Lead utility and transmission owner coordination on facilities and network upgrades, including scope, estimates, transmission-owner-built versus self-built options, engineering reviews, and milestones.
    • Manage Owner’s Engineer and EPC interfaces, define scope boundaries, coordinate long-lead equipment procurement and negotiations, and oversee construction with EPC and engineering teams. Deliver complete packages for construction and commissioning.

Consultant & Vendor Management

  • Write SOWs and manage RFPs, technical and commercial bid evaluation, contracting, purchase orders, invoices, budgets, change management, and closeout.
  • Define deliverables, dependencies, exclusions, and separately priced uncertain tasks. Assess relevant experience and gaps, enforce not-to-exceed estimates, and reject fixed-price or fixed-timeline commitments without documented precedent.
  • Maintain reusable SOW templates, vendor qualification standards, and bid evaluation criteria.

SCADA, Telemetry & Metering

  • Scope and contract SCADA/telemetry engineering; determine responsibility for detailed SCADA/DCS engineering and programming across EPC, integrator, or in-house teams before contracting.
  • Drive novel measurement methods, including translating stored thermal energy into reportable state of charge, through separately scoped, not-to-exceed tasks. Own settlement-quality metering design and validation.
  • Align ICCP configuration and Open Loop/Closed Loop testing with RTO requirements preceding Test Energy and Trial Operation.

Portfolio, Schedule & Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Own integrated schedules, critical paths, dependencies, and milestones. Maintain one portfolio record of deliverables, technical assumptions, open issues, and RTO/TO correspondence.
  • Partner with interconnection/grid engineering, development, execution, product engineering, operations, commercial, legal, and finance teams to align delivery with project commitments. Communicate cost, schedule, and risk to leadership and nontechnical stakeholders; escalate critical-path exposure early.

Key Qualifications

  • 6+ years managing capital energy or electric infrastructure projects—generation, storage, substations, or transmission—with direct accountability for vendor scope, budgets, schedules, and change management.
  • Experience designing interconnection configurations, evaluating feasibility, selecting and procuring equipment, and coordinating interconnection/substation engineering with utilities and transmission owners.
  • Ability to identify gaps in one-line diagrams, protection schemes, point lists, interface control documents, and architecture diagrams.
  • Utility-scale generator experience with SCADA, telemetry, protection and control, or substation automation sufficient to scope work, evaluate bids, and challenge deliverables.
  • Working knowledge of interconnection studies, GIA/LGIA obligations, and the scoping, costing, and construction of interconnection facilities and network upgrades.
  • Strong technical writing and ability to independently manage concurrent projects across geographies and counterparties, navigate ambiguity, prioritize competing deadlines, and raise issues early.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, another engineering discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Additional Qualifications Desired

  • Exposure to ICCP, RTU integration, or RTO telemetry validation, and to resource integration or ICCP modeling teams.
  • Experience with synchronous generator telemetry, settlement-quality metering, and co-located, hybrid, or surplus interconnection configurations.
  • Utility, transmission owner, IPP, or developer-side delivery experience.

Work Location:  Remote, USA

Salary Range:  $163,000 USD - $200,000 USD

Salary Basis:  Annual

Please note that the salary range listed above reflects Antora Energy’s estimated pay for this position. The actual salary offered will be within the posted range and determined based on several factors including but not limited to a candidate’s experiences, credentials and expertise, as they pertain to the position’s requirements.

In addition to a competitive base salary, Antora Energy’s Total Rewards program includes equity compensation in the form of stock options, a premium health benefits package with life and disability insurance, a 401K plan with employer contributions, flexible spending accounts, and an industry leading paid-time-off policy that features flexible and inclusive holiday observance, as well as paid volunteer time off.
